product: Karrot — a skit ad with 5M+ views (the creator's portfolio example; Karrot is the brand).
body: A UGC creator's portfolio post (#13/30): more skit ads lately, excited to film one at a grocery store; throwback to a Karrot skit ad with 5M+ views; pitches skit content services via email. 32s video attached.

"Skit content? I GOT U" plus email.
why_it_works: 5M views is the credential — the portfolio post sells the outcome, not the process.
what_to_steal: Grocery-store-style everyday-location skits for LC — mundane settings make jewelry moments relatable.

product: commentary — no product. A $300k/mo agency's creative strategy; skits among the top-spender wrappers.
body: Agency became top performer in an ad account ($25k/day spend). Step 1: ad account analysis — demographics, trigger events, Facebook comments, winning angles; dissect hooks, narrative, angle, tone, pacing, visuals; connect angles to Life-Force 8 desires. Wrappers that became top spenders (per gist): skits, carpool ads, Suno songs, AI Pixar-character podcasts; hooks must target different people. (Truncated.)
idea: Skits scale to top-spender status on proven angles.
what_to_steal: LC skits as top-spender wrappers for proven angles.

product: commentary — no product. Skits with studio actors as "ads that don't look like ads."
hook: "Just run ads that don't look like ads."
body: Critiques four account-building blocks: identical UGC (Andromeda dedupes 50 near-identical videos into one ad), over-polished ads (dead in frame one), discount statics (train sale-waiting), influencer whitelisting (paying for someone else's audience). The alternative: podcast clips, street interviews, skits with studio actors. Proof: pet brand $29K→$150K/mo spend in 60 days, CPA $188→$124. (Truncated.)
idea: Studio-actor skits are a "doesn't look like an ad" pillar.
what_to_steal: Studio-actor skits for LC's entertainment pillar.
